review_notes: I read the whole file and the related Mathlib uses (Comp.lean, Fix/Cofix, PFunctor M). I compared the simp setup with core's `Functor.map_map`. `id_map` and `id_map'` are sensible simp lemmas. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether adding `@[simp]` to `map_map` would break any downstream `simp` proof. I'm also unsure whether a `⊚` normal form would interact well with the `comp_assoc` and `appendFun_comp` lemmas.

findings.excerpt: theorem map_map (g : α ⟹ β) (h : β ⟹ γ) (x : F α) : h <$$> g <$$> x = (h ⊚ g) <$$> x :=
findings.problem: The `MvFunctor` composition law is stated in the fusing direction, which is the useful one for simp, but it is not tagged `@[simp]`. `id_map` and `id_map'` directly above it are simp, so the functor laws are only half covered. Callers have to pass `MvFunctor.map_map` by name in many `simp` calls. Examples are `simp [MvFunctor.map_map]` in `LiftP_def`, `simp only [map_map, ...]` in `LiftR_def` and `LiftR_RelLast_iff`, and `simp only [... MvFunctor.map_map ...]` in `exists_iff_exists_of_mono`. The same pattern appears in `Comp.lean`. Core's univariate analogue `Functor.map_map` is `@[simp]`. The rewrite is size-decreasing: two maps become one, and the RHS contains no `<$$> ... <$$>` redex that could loop. `comp_map` is the opposite direction, so it should stay non-simp.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `MvFunctor.map_map` with `@[simp]`. Then drop the explicit `MvFunctor.map_map` from `simp [MvFunctor.map_map]` in `LiftP_def` and from the `simp only` lists where it is redundant. Keep `comp_map` non-simp. Check that the `⊚`-normal form still works with the existing `comp_assoc` and `appendFun_comp` simp lemmas.
findings.benefit: Nested `f <$$> g <$$> x` reduces to the canonical single map under plain `simp`, as it does for ordinary `Functor`. Downstream proofs about `LiftP`, `LiftR` and QPF constructions no longer need to name the lemma, and `simp` behaves the same for univariate and multivariate functors.
